name: Question 16
worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}-5x+9}{(x+2)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x+2}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+2)^{3}}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x+2)^{3}$ gives

$$
2{x}^{2}-5x+9=A(x+2)^{2}+B(x+2)+C.
$$

Letting $x=-2$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-2)^{2}-5(-2)+9 & =A(-2+2)^{2}+B(-2+2)+C \\ 27 & =A(0)^{2}+B(0)+C \\ C & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-1$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}-5(-1)+9 & =A(-1+2)^{2}+B(-1+2)+27 \\ 16 & =A+B+27 \\ B & =-A-11.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=0$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)^{2}-5(0)+9 & =A(0+2)^{2}+B(0+2)+27 \\ 9 & =4A+2B+27 \\ 2B & =-4A-18 \\ B & =-2A-9.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-A-11 & =-2A-9 \\ A & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $A$ into $(1)$ to get the value of $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =-2-11 \\ B & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}-5x+9}{(x+2)^{3}}=\frac{2}{x+2}-\frac{13}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{27}{(x+2)^{3}}.
$$
